label: Corporate tax return: deadline after a company's business registration is closed
unit: months from the end of the month in which the fiscal year ends
appliesTo: Companies (법인) that have closed a business registration, as distinct from sole proprietors
why: Because the widely repeated 'file it next May' is the sole-trader rule and does not apply to a company. Sole proprietors settle the closure year through the following May's global income tax return; a company files on its own fiscal-year clock regardless of when the business registration closed. Applying the individual deadline to a company produces a late filing with a penalty attached.

history.display: 3 months from the fiscal year end month
history.source: Corporate Tax Act — filing of the return for each business year
history.note: The return is due within three months from the last day of the month in which the business year ends. Closing the business registration does not extinguish the company: a company that has only stopped trading still exists until it is dissolved and liquidated under the Commercial Act, and a company that is dissolved may have its business year split at the date the dissolution is registered.
